name_ta: Bursa subhyoidea (retrohyoid / Boyer's bursa) -- a descriptive clinical name used in the surgical and anatomical literature; not a separately standardized Terminologia Anatomica entry
clinical_significance: Not tied to a named bursitis syndrome in this atlas's source document; its chief clinical relevance is as a normal closed structure to be recognised as such (rather than mistaken for pathology) on neck ultrasound/imaging near the hyoid-thyrohyoid interval, alongside conditions of the adjacent thyrohyoid membrane and omohyoid sling.
function: Lies between the body of the hyoid bone and the thyrohyoid membrane, allowing the larynx to glide smoothly upward behind the fixed hyoid bone during laryngeal elevation in swallowing and in pitch/register change.
source: Standring S, ed., Gray's Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice, 42nd ed., Elsevier, 2021 -- as cited in this atlas's uploaded head and neck muscle reference document (Head & Neck Muscles -- Clinical Reference v2, Unit 9 note and Thyrohyoid entry)

name_ta: Bursa m. tensoris veli palatini (pterygoid hamulus bursa) -- a descriptive clinical name used in the anatomical literature; not separately standardized in Terminologia Anatomica
name_common: Pterygoid hamulus bursa (tensor veli palatini bursa), right
adjacent_structures: pterygoid hamulus of the sphenoid bone
clinical_significance: No named bursitis syndrome is described for it in this atlas's source document; it is noted there as the only bursa of the soft palate.
function: Cushions the tendon of tensor veli palatini as it turns around the pterygoid hamulus, which acts as its pulley, immediately before the tendon expands into the palatine aponeurosis -- reducing friction as the muscle tenses the soft palate.
source: Standring S, ed., Gray's Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice, 42nd ed., Elsevier, 2021 -- as cited in this atlas's uploaded head and neck muscle reference document (Head & Neck Muscles -- Clinical Reference v2, Unit 6 note and Tensor veli palatini entry)
